key_insight: CAPE extends acoustic perturbation equations to cavitating multiphase flows by embedding vapor mass transfer, mixture compressibility, and pressure-rate effects directly into the source terms.
engineering_relevance: This enables source-resolved prediction of cavitation noise for marine and hydraulic design, helping identify and mitigate tonal and collapse-driven hydroacoustic loads.
method: Formulated cavitation acoustic perturbation equations that couple flow acoustics with phase change physics.
Verified the solver on 1D wave-propagation tests with mesh/time-step refinement and boundary absorption checks.
Applied the framework to a circular cylinder and NACA hydrofoil to isolate vortex-, cavity-shedding, and collapse-related sources.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports grid/time-step-insensitive solutions, effective PML suppression of reflections, and attenuation trends consistent with Stokes' sound attenuation law, plus case studies showing distinct radiation patterns and tonal frequencies.
watch_item: The framework is verified on idealized 1D tests and two canonical geometries, so transfer to fully three-dimensional, highly turbulent cavitating systems may require further validation.
paper_title: Cavitation Acoustic Perturbation Equations: A Computational Framework for Source-Resolved Multiphase Hydroacoustics
